summary.text: Participant 1 was a 57-year-old woman with a hemorrhagic stroke of the left cerebral cortex, right hemiparesis and diminished sensation on the affected side. She had received physical, occupational and speech therapy after the stroke and was a community ambulator with a baseline gait speed of 1.00 m/s. The narrative gives 10 years since the stroke while Table 1 gives 8 years.

She was assigned to sham tDCS combined with VR treadmill gait training, 30-minute sessions five days a week for two consecutive weeks. Pre-intervention scores were 10MWT 1.00 m/s, BBS 49, DGI 11 and TUG 10.18 s; post-intervention scores were 1.22 m/s, 54, 19 and 8.70 s; at the two-week follow up they were 1.35 m/s, 55, 20 and 8.26 s.

Improvements were reported in all measured outcomes from baseline to post-intervention, with DGI and 10MWT described as exceeding the clinically significant threshold, and the other measures stayed consistent at two weeks.

summary.text: Participant 4 was a 69-year-old woman who had an ischemic stroke of the left frontal lobe 12 years earlier, with right hemiparesis affecting motor abilities and functional independence. She was a community ambulator with a baseline gait speed of 1.17 m/s, and her baseline DGI score of 16 was described as predictive of falls.

She was assigned to anodal tDCS with VR treadmill gait training for two consecutive weeks. Pre-intervention scores were 10MWT 1.17 m/s, BBS 44, DGI 16 and TUG 10.23 s; post-intervention 1.32 m/s, 50, 23 and 7.61 s; and at the two-week follow up 1.28 m/s, 55, 23 and 8.06 s.

The narrative reports improvement in all measures post-intervention, a DGI increase of 7 points meeting the clinical improvement threshold, BBS increases of 6 and then 5 points with a clinically significant balance change, non-significant TUG and 10MWT changes, and sustained improvements.

summary.text: Participant 5 was a 29-year-old man seven years after a hemorrhagic basal ganglia stroke, with right hemiparesis, noticeable right arm tremors, an ankle-foot orthosis on the right leg and walking with a service animal. He had undergone occupational and speech therapy, was in aquatic therapy once a week and was a community ambulator with a baseline gait speed of 1.19 m/s.

He was assigned to sham tDCS with VR treadmill gait training for two consecutive weeks. Pre-intervention scores were 10MWT 1.19 m/s, BBS 52, DGI 16 and TUG 8.87 s; post-intervention scores were 1.57 m/s, 55, 22 and 7.51 s.

He was withdrawn at the two-week follow-up because of an unrelated hospitalization and no data were recorded. Improvement was noted in all assessments immediately after the intervention, with clinical significance reported only for DGI and 10MWT, and he found the game motivating.
